newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds set to go on rising, echoing Germany.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds set to go on rising, echoing Germany.

text.p: Danish bonds rose slightly on Wednesday, echoing German technical gains and dealers predicted that the trend would continue for the rest of the day.
"We are set to follow this morning's technical gains in Germany up until the close," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up 0.17 point from the start at 112.93, yielding 6.04 percent, while the forthcoming seven percent 2007 benchmark rose 0.20 point to 105.60 with the yield at 6.25 percent. The 2007-bund yield gap widened one basis point to 61 bps during the course of the morning.
Dealers said the market was focused on FOMC and U.S. June job data expected on Thursday.

Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 benchmarks was 1.8 and 1.5 billion crowns respectively. The 2006's September future rose 0.38 point to 112.10 with nine contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.25 point to 91.20.

The crown traded at a virtually unchanged 3.8068 per mark at 1130 gmt. The Central Bank was active on the market selling some 500 million crowns worth of medium and long-term bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
